title: Private Pilot FAR Knowledge
description: Test your knowledge of Federal Aviation Regulations for Private Pilots

questions.question: What is the minimum age requirement to obtain a private pilot certificate for an airplane?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 61.103, an applicant for a private pilot certificate must be at least 17 years of age (or 16 for glider or balloon).

questions.question: How often must a flight review be accomplished to act as pilot in command?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 61.56, no person may act as pilot in command unless within the preceding 24 calendar months they have accomplished a flight review.

questions.question: To carry passengers at night, a pilot must have made at least how many takeoffs and landings within the preceding 90 days?
options: 3 takeoffs and 3 landings to a full stop
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 61.57, to carry passengers at night, a pilot must have made 3 takeoffs and 3 landings to a full stop during the period beginning 1 hour after sunset and ending 1 hour before sunrise within the preceding 90 days.

questions.question: What minimum flight visibility is required for VFR flight in Class B airspace?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.155, the minimum flight visibility for VFR flight in Class B airspace is 3 statute miles.

questions.question: What is the maximum indicated airspeed permitted below 10,000 feet MSL?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.117, no person may operate an aircraft below 10,000 feet MSL at an indicated airspeed of more than 250 knots.

questions.question: When must a pilot have a current medical certificate to exercise private pilot privileges?
options: Only when carrying passengers for hire
questions.explanation: A pilot must have a current medical certificate unless operating under BasicMed, which requires meeting specific requirements outlined in 14 CFR 61.23 and 68.

questions.question: What is the minimum fuel reserve required for day VFR flight?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.151, no person may begin a VFR flight during the day unless there is enough fuel to fly to the first point of intended landing and, assuming normal cruising speed, to fly after that for at least 30 minutes.

questions.question: What is the minimum fuel reserve required for night VFR flight?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.151, for night VFR flight, there must be enough fuel to fly to the first point of intended landing and to fly after that for at least 45 minutes at normal cruising speed.

questions.question: Who is responsible for determining that an aircraft is in condition for safe flight?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.7, the pilot in command of a civil aircraft is responsible for determining whether that aircraft is in condition for safe flight.

questions.question: What action should be taken if a pilot deviates from an ATC instruction in an emergency?
options: File a NASA report within 10 days
Submit a written report upon request
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.123, each pilot who is given priority by ATC in an emergency shall submit a detailed report of that emergency within 48 hours to the manager of that ATC facility, if requested by ATC.

questions.question: What is the minimum altitude for flight over congested areas?
options: 1,000 feet above the highest obstacle within 2,000 feet horizontal
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.119, over congested areas, aircraft must maintain an altitude of 1,000 feet above the highest obstacle within a horizontal radius of 2,000 feet.

questions.question: How long after consuming alcohol may a person act as a flight crewmember?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.17, no person may act as a crewmember within 8 hours after the consumption of any alcoholic beverage.

questions.question: What is the maximum blood alcohol content allowed to act as a crewmember?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.17, no person may act as a crewmember while having 0.04 percent by weight or more alcohol in the blood.

questions.question: When two aircraft are approaching each other head-on, each pilot should:
options: Climb to avoid the other aircraft
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.113, when aircraft are approaching head-on or nearly so, each pilot shall alter course to the right.

questions.question: Which aircraft has the right-of-way over all other traffic?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.113, an aircraft in distress has the right-of-way over all other air traffic.

questions.question: How often must an aircraft's transponder be tested and inspected?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.413, the transponder must be tested and inspected within the preceding 24 calendar months.

questions.question: When must an Emergency Locator Transmitter (ELT) be inspected?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.207, an ELT must be inspected within 12 calendar months after the last inspection.

questions.question: When must position lights be displayed on an aircraft?
options: When visibility is less than 3 miles
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.209, no person may operate an aircraft from sunset to sunrise unless the aircraft has lighted position lights.

questions.question: What is the required equipment for VFR flight during the day? (Remember: ATOMATOFLAMES)
options: Attitude indicator, transponder, oil pressure gauge
Airspeed indicator, altimeter, magnetic compass, fuel gauge, oil temperature gauge
Gyroscopic heading indicator, attitude indicator, turn coordinator
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.205, day VFR requires airspeed indicator, altimeter, magnetic compass (direction indicator), tachometer, oil pressure gauge, manifold pressure gauge (if applicable), oil/temperature gauges, fuel gauges, landing gear indicator, anticollision lights, ELT, and safety belts.

questions.question: What cloud clearance is required for VFR flight in Class E airspace below 10,000 feet MSL?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.155, VFR flight in Class E airspace below 10,000 feet MSL requires 500 feet below clouds, 1,000 feet above clouds, and 2,000 feet horizontal from clouds.

questions.question: A private pilot may share expenses equally with passengers for:
options: Fuel, oil, airport expenditures, and aircraft rental fees
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 61.113, a private pilot may not pay less than the pro rata share of the operating expenses of a flight with passengers, provided the expenses involve only fuel, oil, airport expenditures, or rental fees.

questions.question: At what altitude must the altimeter be set to 29.92 inches Hg?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.121, at or above 18,000 feet MSL, the altimeter must be set to 29.92 inches Hg (standard pressure).

questions.question: What action is required before entering Class C airspace?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.130, pilots must establish two-way radio communication with ATC before entering Class C airspace.

questions.question: What action is required before entering Class B airspace?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.131, pilots must receive an ATC clearance from the ATC facility having jurisdiction before operating in Class B airspace.

questions.question: What type of aircraft operations are allowed in Class A airspace?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.135, unless otherwise authorized, each person operating an aircraft in Class A airspace must operate under instrument flight rules (IFR).

questions.question: How many hours of flight time are required for a private pilot certificate (airplane single-engine land)?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 61.109, a person who applies for a private pilot certificate with an airplane category and single-engine class rating must log at least 40 hours of flight time.

questions.question: What is required to fly a high-performance airplane?
options: A logbook endorsement from an authorized instructor
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 61.31, a pilot must have received and logged ground and flight training in a high-performance airplane and received a logbook endorsement from an authorized instructor.

questions.question: What defines a high-performance airplane?
options: An airplane with an engine of more than 200 horsepower
An airplane with a maximum gross weight over 12,500 lbs
An airplane capable of flight above FL250
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 61.31, a high-performance airplane is an airplane with an engine of more than 200 horsepower.

questions.question: What defines a complex airplane?
options: An airplane with an engine of more than 200 horsepower
An airplane with retractable gear, flaps, and controllable pitch propeller
An airplane requiring a type rating
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 61.31, a complex airplane has retractable landing gear, flaps, and a controllable pitch propeller.

questions.question: How often must a 100-hour inspection be performed on an aircraft used for hire?
options: Every 100 hours of time in service
Every 100 hours or annual, whichever comes first
Every 200 hours of time in service
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.409, aircraft used for hire or flight instruction for hire must have a 100-hour inspection performed every 100 hours of time in service.

questions.question: By how many hours may the 100-hour inspection be exceeded?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.409, the 100-hour limitation may be exceeded by not more than 10 hours while en route to a place where the inspection can be done.

questions.question: What documents must be on board an aircraft during flight?
options: Airworthiness certificate, registration certificate, operating limitations, and weight and balance data
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.9 and 91.203, the aircraft must have its airworthiness certificate, registration certificate, and operating limitations (AFM, POH, placards). Weight and balance information must also be available.

questions.question: Where must the airworthiness certificate be displayed?
options: At the cabin or cockpit entrance
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.203, the airworthiness certificate must be displayed at the cabin or cockpit entrance so that it is legible to passengers or crew.

questions.question: What is the validity period of a third-class medical certificate for a pilot under 40 years old?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 61.23, a third-class medical certificate is valid for 60 calendar months for operations requiring a third-class medical for persons under 40 years of age.

questions.question: What is the validity period of a third-class medical certificate for a pilot 40 years old or older?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 61.23, a third-class medical certificate is valid for 24 calendar months for operations requiring a third-class medical for persons 40 years of age or older.

questions.question: When may a private pilot log second-in-command (SIC) time?
options: Any time they are the sole manipulator of the controls
When required by the type certificate or regulations
During any flight with another pilot
Never, only commercial pilots can log SIC time
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 61.51, a pilot may log SIC time when the pilot serves as SIC of an aircraft on which more than one pilot is required under the type certificate or regulations.

questions.question: What must a pilot do before a flight not in the vicinity of an airport?
options: Become familiar with all available information concerning the flight
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.103, each pilot in command shall become familiar with all available information concerning that flight before beginning a flight.

questions.question: What color is a steady light signal meaning 'cleared to land' for aircraft in flight?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.125, a steady green light signal to an aircraft in flight means 'cleared to land.'

questions.question: What color is a flashing red light signal to an aircraft on the surface?
options: Taxi clear of runway in use
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.125, a flashing red light signal to an aircraft on the surface means 'taxi clear of runway in use.'

questions.question: At what altitudes must supplemental oxygen be used by the crew?
options: Above 10,000 feet MSL for more than 30 minutes
Above 12,500 feet MSL for more than 30 minutes
Above 14,000 feet MSL at all times
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.211, required crew must use supplemental oxygen above 12,500 feet up to 14,000 feet for more than 30 minutes, and above 14,000 feet at all times.

questions.question: At what altitude must supplemental oxygen be provided to passengers?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.211, above 15,000 feet MSL, each occupant must be provided with supplemental oxygen.

questions.question: What is the maximum indicated airspeed in a Class D airspace underlying Class B airspace?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.117, the maximum indicated airspeed when operating beneath the lateral limits of Class B airspace is 200 knots.

questions.question: What is required to act as pilot in command of an aircraft carrying passengers?
options: 3 takeoffs and landings in the preceding 90 days
A flight review in the preceding 12 months
A practical test in the preceding 24 months
An instrument proficiency check in the preceding 6 months
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 61.57, to carry passengers, a pilot must have made at least 3 takeoffs and 3 landings within the preceding 90 days in the same category, class, and type of aircraft.

questions.question: In an emergency, the pilot in command may:
options: Deviate from any rule to the extent required
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.3, in an in-flight emergency requiring immediate action, the pilot in command may deviate from any rule of Part 91 to the extent required to meet that emergency.

questions.question: What is the definition of 'night' for logging night flight time?
options: One hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
End of evening civil twilight to beginning of morning civil twilight
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 1.1, night means the time between the end of evening civil twilight and the beginning of morning civil twilight.

questions.question: Who may perform preventive maintenance on an aircraft?
options: Only certified mechanics with IA authorization
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 43.3, a pilot may perform preventive maintenance on any aircraft owned or operated by that pilot (not for hire).

questions.question: How long must aircraft maintenance records be retained for the airframe, engine, and propeller?
options: 1 year after the work is performed
5 years after the work is performed
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.417, airframe, engine, and propeller records must be retained until the work is superseded by work of equivalent scope and detail.

questions.question: What minimum pilot certificate is required to operate in Class B airspace?
options: Student with instructor endorsement at some locations
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.131, a private pilot certificate is generally required, but student pilots may operate at some Class B airports with specific endorsements. Certain Class B primary airports prohibit student pilots.

questions.question: What is the minimum flight visibility required for Special VFR during the day?
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.157, Special VFR requires at least 1 statute mile flight visibility and clear of clouds during the day.

questions.question: What additional requirement applies for Special VFR operations at night?
options: Pilot must be instrument rated and aircraft instrument equipped
questions.explanation: Under 14 CFR 91.157, for Special VFR operations at night, the pilot must be instrument rated and the aircraft must be IFR equipped.
